column1: # Operating system functions. One row per function, per task it belongs to. Tab-separated; see finder.py for the rules.

column7: summary
Returns command-line argument n, the program's name for 0, or all of them if omitted.
Runs a command through the system shell, waits, and returns its exit code or -1.
Runs a program by its path with arguments, waits, and returns its exit code or -1.
Runs a program without arguments, waits, and returns its exit code or -1.
Hands control to another program and ends this one; returns -1 if it cannot start.
Returns the value of an environment variable, or an empty string if it is not set.
Sets an environment variable from "NAME=value" text; returns 0 on success.
Returns the folder that holds the running program.
Returns the current folder.
Changes the current folder; returns 0 on success or -1 on failure.
Creates one folder, whose parent must already exist; returns 0 on success.
Removes an empty folder; returns 0 on success or -1 on failure.
Returns the first name matching a pattern, then the next one on each later call.
Copies a file, overwriting the destination; returns 0 on success.
Renames or moves a file or folder; returns 0 on success.
Deletes a file; returns 0 on success or an error code.
Returns non-zero if the file exists, or 0 if it does not.
Returns the size of a named file in bytes.
Returns when a file was last modified, as a date serial.
Returns an open file number's mode, system handle or encoding.
Writes buffered output for one or all open files to the system, or on to disk.
Cuts or extends an open file so that it ends at the current position.
Closes all open files and ends the program, with an optional exit code.
Returns the amount of free physical memory, in bytes.
Returns non-zero if standard output, or input if asked, is redirected to a file.
